reply_text:
Now the routes doc (rule 1 and a topo3 section), then commit.㊥ ("spin up a third HEAVY loop") topo3 is running (`33ecc2a1`). It covers the 19 registered HEAVY problems no loop was allowed to work on, 41 placeholders between them. Its first strategy checkpoint is running on topo-12. topo1 and topo2 restarted alongside it.

㊢ (setup)
- **Problems:** t00A02, t00A03, t00J02, t01A08, t01J01, t02A04, t03J02, t03J03, t91J05, t92J05, t94J04, t95J06, t96A01, t96A02, t96J06, t97A05, t97A06, t97J02, t98A02. That's the unassigned HEAVY list minus the 14 topo1 took in its two refills, keeping only problems with registered statements and placeholders left.
- **Loop:** unit `topo3`, ledger `worklist3.edn`, logs in `runs3/`. Seats are topo-9 (owner), topo-10 (author and repair), topo-11 (review) and topo-12 (probe and strategy), all registered on sol.
- **Seed checkpoint:** builds topo3's lemma DAG from these problems' routes, tagged by area, plus the open nodes of the old DAG that bear on them. It then elects by area reach, starting with surface-classification (7 of these problems) and mayer-vietoris-open-cover (5).
- **Docs and tools:** `TOPOLOGY-ROUTES.md` rule 1 and a new topo3 section; `build_step.bb areas` now reads all three ledgers.
- **Watch:** now covers topo3 as well (`bg-1791669753855-433`).

㊩ (quota) Codex weekly use is at 60%, up from 44% at 16:33, so two loops were using about 3 points an hour. Three loops should use about 4.5 an hour, which leaves roughly 9 hours before the first reset. When a loop stops on quota, the watch pages you through zone-notify.

㊬ (progress) Placeholders went from 153 to 151 since 16:33, the first drop since the restart. Closed problems are still at 63.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(how it works)
- **Where areas come from:** an area is either a shared tag from the problem tables in `TOPOLOGY-ROUTES.md`, which already tag all 71 problems, or a lemma's own `:area`. A banked lemma without a tag falls under the ConstructionTargets module its commit wrote.
- **`build_step.bb areas`** (also printed at the end of `priorities`) lists each area with the open registered problems it serves (including the other loop's and unassigned ones), its banked and backlog lemmas, and its modules.
- **Lemma ranking:** among lemmas that are ready to build, the one in the wider area now comes first. Lemmas take `:area` from receipts, and the first spelling is kept.
- **Strategy prompt:** at most one closure-directed row per checkpoint. The other slots go to the highest-impact areas that serve at least one of the loop's own problems, with each area's results built once, in one ConstructionTargets module. Untagged lemmas get tagged as they come up; right now most of the backlog is untagged, so area counts will fill in over the next few checkpoints.

previous_reply_acts.text: (checked) Tagging through `add-lemmas` validates and shows up in `areas`. Both live ledgers validate, the lab tests pass, and nobody else had edited the files I replaced.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-14
previous_reply_acts.text: (wide areas outside both loops) The widest areas belong mostly to problems neither loop is allowed to work on. **surface-classification** serves 7 open problems (t00A02, t00A03, t91J05, t92J05, t94J04, t96A01, t97J02), and **mayer-vietoris-open-cover** serves 5. All 7 surface-classification problems and most of the Mayer–Vietoris ones are on the unassigned HEAVY list. Election rule 1 limits each loop to its own problem list, so the loops can see these areas but won't build them. Should a loop be assigned areas, such as surface classification, rather than only a fixed list of problems?
